name: Adam

team.summary: Zach, part of YC batch W25, building Adam with technical open-source shipping approach.

product.summary: CADAM, an open-source Text to CAD platform running fully in-browser using WebAssembly and Three.js, generating OpenSCAD code with interactive parameter sliders.

market.summary: Mechanical design and CAD software users, developers, and engineers looking for AI-assisted 3D modeling.

risks.risk: Current LLMs have poor spatial awareness and struggle with technical accuracy and functional requirements for manufacturing.
OpenSCAD is viewed by some engineers as insufficient for serious production-grade mechanical design compared to constraint-driven modeling.

founder_depth.why: Founder is technical, shipping in public (W25), open-sourcing the core repo, and detailing specific architectural choices like WASM compilation and Vercel AI SDK integration.

shipping_evidence.why: High GitHub traction with 5,134 stars, live working demo, and active commit history up to September 2026.

demand_signal.why: HN post gained 215 points and 97 comments with strong initial user engagement, positive feedback on simple tasks, alongside heavy technical skepticism.

defensibility.why: Open-source codebase wrapping standard models via Vercel AI SDK with limited current moat discussed beyond UX polish and parametric slider regex updates.

analysis.verdict_reason: Strong technical execution and impressive developer traction (5k+ stars) for an open-source AI dev tool, despite valid domain-specific engineering skepticism.
would_change_my_mind: Demonstrating integration with professional geometry kernels or constraint-driven modeling like CadQuery/build123d
Evidence of production-grade usage where generated parts pass manufacturing tolerances
A clear path to commercial monetization beyond the open-source repo
data_gaps: Revenue model or commercialization plans for adam.new
Exact breakdown of active enterprise vs hobbyist users
